title: American hunter involved in Sask. crash that killed mom and two daughters leaving Canada on bail
summary: Kelly Knopf is out on bail. He has a broken pelvis and will return to South Carolina for treatment of injuries sustained in the Oct. 2 crash, his lawyer said in a statement.

image.caption: Amber Olson and Shaun Didychuk with their daughters, Isla and Everly, in an undated photo. Olson and her daughters died in the crash. (Submitted by Cassandra Pendlebury)

blocks.text: Kelly Knopf is out on bail. He has a broken pelvis and will return to South Carolina for treatment of injuries sustained in the Oct. 2 crash, his lawyer said in a statement.
Kelly Knopf will seek medical treatment in South Carolina, his lawyer says

An American man facing charges after a crash in Saskatchewan that killed a mother and her two daughters was released Thursday on $20,000 bail and will return to the United States, his lawyer told CBC News.
The Oct. 2 crash happened near Foam Lake, about 200 kilometres northeast of Regina.
Kelly Knopf, 40, has a broken pelvis and will return to South Carolina to seek medical treatment, Brian Pfefferle, his Saskatoon-based lawyer, said in a statement.

items: Sask. town mourns mom, 2 girls killed in crash with U.S. hunter

blocks.text: "This is a terrible tragedy and Mr. Knopf intends to comply with the conditions and is grateful the Crown agreed to his release," Pfefferle said.
Knopf is charged with multiple counts of dangerous driving causing death and dangerous driving causing bodily harm.

items: Woman, 2 children dead after serious collision near Foam Lake, Sask.

blocks.text: Amber Olson, 40, and her daughters Isla and Everly , ages five and eight, died in the collision. Shaun Didychuk, the girls' father, was taken to hospital with serious injuries.
In a previous statement, Pfefferle said Knopf came to Canada on a hunting trip.

Maeve Ellis is a reporter and associate producer with CBC News based in Saskatoon. You can reach her at maeve.ellis@cbc.ca or maeveellis_ on X. She would love to hear from anyone with Sask-related story ideas.
With files from Alexander Quon and Randi LaRocque.
